messages:
jordan: BlueNova asked for a 3-week POC. Requirements: isolated VPC (no outbound), websocket streaming with backpressure, function/tool-calling to their internal payment-validate gRPC, structured JSONL export to their SFTP daily, SAML SSO + HSM/KMS, and SOC2 compliance artifacts. They want a one-page estimate + a simple demo showing tool calls over stream. Any immediate red flags?

priya: A couple quick clarifiers: 1) isolated VPC = full airgap or can we run a control plane inside their VPC that phones home for licensing? 2) SFTP export: push or pull? 3) target concurrency/p95? 4) do they need model weight residency or is a quantized local copy ok?

jordan: Answers from customer: 1) no phone home, local control plane only. 2) push to their SFTP nightly. 3) steady 10 RPS, spikes to 80 RPS, p95 <400ms for short prompts. 4) local quantized weights are fine.

diego: Ok. Offline control plane + model tarball required. For tool calls we ship a lightweight adapter that exposes a local HTTP shim for the runtime to call, which then forwards to their gRPC service inside the VPC. Suggest containerized adapter + systemd unit for stability. For streaming use websocket with chunked events and client backpressure. Watch KV cache size on smaller nodes.

priya: Sample streaming client snippet (to demo): ```python
from redwood import StreamingClient
client = StreamingClient(endpoint='wss://local-redwood:443', token='EPHEMERAL')
with client.stream(session_id='bn-demo') as s:
    s.send({"input":"validate txn 987","tool_call":"payment_check"})
    for event in s.recv():
        if event.get('tool_call_response'):
            print('tool reply:', event['tool_call_response'])
        else:
            print('chunk:', event['text'])
```

diego: Minimal tool schema (YAML) for adapter: ```yaml
name: payment_check
inputs:
  - name: txn_id
    type: string
outputs:
  - name: verdict
    type: string
endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:60051/validate # adapter forwards to gRPC
```

security-bot: Security checklist created: https://redwood.internal/security/onprem-checklist (internal) 

priya: SAML note: if BlueNova requires IdP-initiated login for the admin console we need their metadata and a test IdP. Also they'll need ephemeral tokens for SDKs (we recommend 2-5m rotation backed by their HSM).

deploy-bot: Ports doc: https://redwood.internal/infra/onprem-ports. Suggested: 443 (control plane), 50051 (adapter internal), and 22/873 for SFTP ops (if allowed).

jordan: Pricing: they asked for delta vs hosted for 3-week POC. Can we give a sticker?

diego: Quick ballpark for presales: onprem POC bundle: $30k one-time license + $2.5k model transfer + $9k eng support (6 eng-days: SE+infra+runtime). If we add fast adapter customization ~2 days = +$3k. If they accept containerized adapter only we can discount ~20%. Mention travel? none (remote).

priya: I'll draft a 3-week runbook (fast path: container adapter + example SFTP exporter; full path: custom adapter + SAML integration + audit log retention) and a one-page estimate. Will also prep the demo repo with the streaming + toolcall stub.

jordan: Can someone drop a minimal curl demo we can run locally in 24h for their devs? Need to show streaming + tool invocation.

diego: Quick curl demo (pseudo): ```bash
# start local adapter and control plane (presales container)
docker run --rm -p 443:443 redwood/onprem-presales:latest &
./redwood-adapter --listen 127.0.0.1:50051 --tool-schema ./payment_check.yaml &
# trigger stream with tool call
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer EPHEMERAL" -N \
  -d '{"input":"validate txn 987","stream":true,"tool_call":"payment_check"}' \
  https://localhost/api/v1/generate
```

priya: Great — I'll wrap that into a tiny repo and include a README and a network diagram template for them to fill. Jordan, I'll send the estimate + demo link by tomorrow morning.

jordan: Perfect. Action items: Priya = one-pager + demo repo; Diego = quick adapter container + payment_check.yaml; Security-bot = share onprem checklist; Deploy-bot = ports link. Aim to have materials for kickoff this week. :thumbsup:
